questions.prompt: A Python app on Flex Consumption is deployed from a CI pipeline, and its packages must be installed in Azure. How is the remote build requested?

options.text: With ENABLE_ORYX_BUILD set to true in the app settings
With the remoteBuild parameter passed when the deployment starts
With WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE set to a remote package URL
With SCM_DO_BUILD_DURING_DEPLOYMENT set to true in the app settings

questions.explanation: On Flex Consumption, a remote build is requested by passing the remote build parameter when a code-package deployment starts, and it isn't configured through application settings. SCM_DO_BUILD_DURING_DEPLOYMENT and ENABLE_ORYX_BUILD are deprecated there, replaced by that remoteBuild parameter, and WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE isn't used for Flex Consumption deployments.

questions.prompt: Complete the az functionapp create command for a Flex Consumption app with 4 GB instances and warm HTTP capacity.

slots.text: Instance size: --instance-memory ____
Keep two instances ready for the HTTP functions: --always-ready-instances ____

options.text: function:http=2
http=2
all=2

slots.text: Region of the Flex Consumption app: ____ westeurope

options.text: --consumption-plan-location
--plan-location
--flexconsumption-location

questions.explanation: Flex Consumption offers 512, 2,048 and 4,096 MB instances, so 4 GB instances are 4096. Always-ready counts for the HTTP group use the group name http, while function:<name>=n is for a single function outside the groups, and there's no all group. The region of a Flex Consumption app is given with --flexconsumption-location, whereas --consumption-plan-location belongs to the legacy Consumption plan.

questions.prompt: You plan to move an existing Premium plan app to Flex Consumption. Which TWO facts shape the move? Select TWO.

options.text: A new app and a redeploy, since in-place migration isn't supported
Deployment slots carry over, so staged releases keep working as before
PowerShell managed dependencies keep working with no changes
The app keeps its 32-bit worker process setting after the move
Content-share settings such as WEBSITE_CONTENTSHARE have to be left out

questions.explanation: In-place migration to or from Flex Consumption isn't supported, so you create a new Flex Consumption app and redeploy the code, and settings such as WEBSITE_CONTENTSHARE are deprecated there and shouldn't be used. Deployment slots aren't supported, 32-bit workers aren't available, and PowerShell managed dependencies have to be replaced by modules uploaded with the app content.

questions.prompt: Which TWO statements about function timeouts are true? Select TWO.

options.text: Dedicated plans enforce a 60-minute maximum timeout
The default functionTimeout on Flex Consumption and Premium is 30 minutes
The legacy Consumption plan allows at most 10 minutes
An HTTP-triggered function can respond for as long as functionTimeout allows
The language worker process gets 10 minutes to start

questions.explanation: The default timeout is 30 minutes on Flex Consumption, Premium, Dedicated and Container Apps, with no enforced maximum, while the legacy Consumption plan defaults to 5 minutes and stops at 10. An HTTP-triggered function still has to respond within 230 seconds whatever the timeout, the language worker has 60 seconds to start, and a Dedicated plan with Always On has no maximum.

questions.prompt: A function app must reach its host storage account with its system-assigned identity instead of a connection string. Which change is needed?

options.text: Set AzureWebJobsStorage__accountName and give the identity Storage Blob Data Owner
Set AzureWebJobsStorage__clientId and give the identity Storage Blob Data Reader
Set AzureWebJobsStorage to the account's name and give the identity the Reader role on it
Keep AzureWebJobsStorage and give the identity Storage Account Contributor

questions.explanation: For host storage, an identity-based connection uses AzureWebJobsStorage__accountName, a syntax unique to this setting, in place of the connection string, and Learn names Storage Blob Data Owner as the minimum role the host needs, with Storage Table Data Contributor added for diagnostic events. The clientId property selects a user-assigned identity, Blob Data Reader can't write the host's blobs, and keeping the connection string leaves the secret in place.

questions.prompt: A Flex Consumption app has zone redundancy enabled, and a setting of one always-ready instance for its http group is rejected. Why?

options.text: Zone-redundant apps can't use always-ready instances at all
With zone redundancy, each group needs at least two always-ready instances
Always-ready counts can be set on single functions only, not on groups
The http group first needs a maximum instance count of at least 2

questions.explanation: Learn says you can configure no fewer than two always-ready instances per function or function group while zone redundancy is enabled, so the http group needs a count of 2 or more. Always-ready instances work with zone redundancy, the http, blob and durable groups take always-ready counts by group name, and the maximum instance count limits only on-demand instances.

questions.prompt: For each statement about Flex Consumption apps, select Yes or No.

options.text: Yes
No

slots.text: Two apps that share a deployment storage account should each use their own container.
Mounted Azure Files shares authenticate with a storage account access key.
The instance memory size can be set only when the app is created.
App initialization has a configurable timeout of up to 10 minutes.

questions.explanation: Learn says each app should use its own deployment container so that packages aren't overwritten, and Azure Files mounts authenticate with the storage account access key. The instance memory size can be changed at any time, for example with az functionapp scale config set, while app initialization times out after 30 seconds and that timeout can't be configured.

questions.prompt: Match each hosting plan to how Learn says to deploy a locally built package to it.

options.text: An FTPS upload to the app's wwwroot folder
Package deployment with no WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE setting
ZIP deployment with WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE set to 1
An external package URL in WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE

slots.text: Flex Consumption plan
Premium plan
Consumption plan on Linux (legacy, retiring)

questions.explanation: Flex Consumption runs from the package it keeps in its deployment container, and Learn says not to set WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE there. Premium, like Dedicated and Windows Consumption, uses ZIP deployment with WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE=1, and for a locally built package on Linux Consumption, a legacy plan that retires in September 2028, the route is an external package URL. For FTPS, Learn says don't use this deployment method.

questions.prompt: Put the steps in order to run a new Linux Premium app from an external package URL; the app's managed identity can already read the blob container.

options.text: Upload the package to a private blob container
Build a .zip deployment package of the project
Restart the app and sync its triggers
Add WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE with the blob's URL as its value

questions.explanation: The package has to exist and sit in the container before its URL can go into WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE, and with an external package URL the trigger metadata isn't updated automatically, so Learn ends with a restart and a manual trigger sync. Reading the private blob with the managed identity avoids SAS tokens, which expire.

questions.prompt: An ARM template for a new Flex Consumption app sets FUNCTIONS_WORKER_RUNTIME to python. What does Learn say about this setting on that plan?

options.text: It has to be paired with WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE=1
It's required, because the plan can't detect the worker language
It's deprecated, and the language goes in functionAppConfig instead
It's ignored unless FUNCTIONS_EXTENSION_VERSION is also set in the template

questions.explanation: On Flex Consumption, FUNCTIONS_WORKER_RUNTIME is among the deprecated settings: the language goes in the name of properties.functionAppConfig.runtime, with the version beside it. FUNCTIONS_EXTENSION_VERSION is managed by the platform and shouldn't be set, and WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE isn't used for Flex Consumption deployments.

questions.prompt: A rotation function's managed identity must read a secret and write new versions of it in one vault, with no rights on keys or certificates. Which built-in role should it get at vault scope?

options.text: Key Vault Secrets User
Key Vault Contributor
Key Vault Administrator
Key Vault Secrets Officer

questions.explanation: Key Vault Secrets Officer allows any action on a vault's secrets except managing permissions, which covers reading the current value and adding new versions. Key Vault Administrator also opens keys and certificates, Key Vault Secrets User can read secret contents but can't write them, and Key Vault Contributor manages the vault resource without any access to its data.

questions.prompt: A function must rotate a secret automatically some time before the secret's expiration date. Which Key Vault event type should its Event Grid subscription filter on?

options.text: Microsoft.KeyVault.SecretNewVersionCreated
Microsoft.KeyVault.VaultAccessPolicyChanged
Microsoft.KeyVault.SecretExpired
Microsoft.KeyVault.SecretNearExpiry

questions.explanation: Key Vault publishes SecretNearExpiry 30 days before the current version's expiration date, which leaves an Event Grid-triggered function time to create and store the replacement. SecretExpired arrives after the version has already expired, SecretNewVersionCreated fires once a version is written (so the rotation itself would trigger it), and VaultAccessPolicyChanged reports access policy or permission model changes.

questions.prompt: A security review asks you to cut the soft-delete retention of an existing vault from 90 days to 30. What should you do?

options.text: Create a new vault with a 30-day retention and move the secrets to it
Run az keyvault update on the vault with a 30-day retention value
Turn soft-delete off on the vault, then on again with a 30-day period
Enable purge protection, which shortens the retention period to 30 days

questions.explanation: The retention interval, anywhere from 7 to 90 days, is chosen when a vault is created and can't be changed later, so a shorter period means a new vault. Once soft-delete is on it can't be switched off, and purge protection uses the vault's existing retention interval instead of setting a new one.

questions.prompt: Complete the azure-keyvault-secrets code that a rotation job runs with its managed identity.

slots.text: client = SecretClient(vault_url=VAULT_URL, credential=____)

options.text: DefaultAzureCredential()
os.environ["KEY_VAULT_NAME"]
f"https://{name}.vault.azure.net"

slots.text: Write the new password as the latest version: client.____("db-password", new_password)

options.text: set_secret
list_properties_of_secrets
update_secret_properties

slots.text: Read back what callers now receive: client.get_secret("db-password").____

options.text: value
name
properties.version

questions.explanation: SecretClient takes the vault URL and a credential object, and DefaultAzureCredential picks up the managed identity in Azure and the developer's sign-in locally; the vault name and URL are inputs, not credentials. set_secret adds a new version when the name already exists, whereas update_secret_properties changes metadata alone and list_properties_of_secrets returns properties without values. The secret's content is in .value, while .name and .properties.version identify it.

questions.prompt: A secret was deleted by mistake from a vault that has purge protection turned on. Which TWO statements are true? Select TWO.

options.text: Purge protection doubles the retention period, to 180 days at most
A user with Key Vault Purge Operator can purge the deleted secret right away
get_secret still returns its value until the secret is purged
A new secret with its name can't be created while it's in the deleted state
Purging it is blocked until the retention period has passed

questions.explanation: With purge protection on, a deleted object can't be purged before the retention period ends, whoever asks, although it can still be recovered. While a secret sits in the deleted state its name stays taken in that vault, and retrieval calls fail because a deleted object can be listed, recovered or purged but not read. Purge protection reuses the vault's 7 to 90 day retention interval instead of extending it.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of a two-key rotation, for a storage account key kept as a Key Vault secret, in order.

options.text: Event Grid delivers the vault's event to the rotation function
The function reads the latest secret version's tags to see which key it holds
The function regenerates the other key in the storage account
The function adds the regenerated key to the vault as the secret's new latest version

questions.explanation: The latest version holds the key that apps use now, so the function first checks which key that is and then regenerates the alternate one, which no app depends on. Storing that key as the new latest version moves apps to it on their next read, while the key they had stays valid for a whole cycle until it becomes the alternate.

questions.prompt: docs-worker reads the Azure OpenAI key from Key Vault for every job and gets HTTP 429 responses during upload bursts. What should Contoso change?

options.text: Cache the key in memory and reread it once calls start failing
Build the key into the docs-worker image during each release
Read a pinned version of the secret on each job, not the latest
Retry each throttled read at once until Key Vault returns the key

questions.explanation: Key Vault's service limits aren't designed for a read per message, and its guidance is to cache retrieved secrets in memory and read them again when the cached copy stops working, for example after a rotation. The guidance also says to avoid immediate retries and to back off exponentially after a 429; a key in the image breaks Contoso's rule against secrets in images, and a pinned version is still one call per job.

questions.prompt: A deleted vault was recovered within its retention period. Since then its apps get 403 errors, and its rotation function no longer receives events. What explains this?

options.text: The recovered vault was given a new DNS name, so the old vault URI fails
A recovered vault stays read-only until its original retention period ends
Recovery switched soft-delete off, and the vault blocks access until it's on again
Recovery restored neither the role assignments nor the Event Grid subscription

questions.explanation: Soft-deleting a vault also deletes the services integrated with it, such as Azure RBAC role assignments and Event Grid subscriptions, and recovering the vault doesn't bring them back, so both have to be created again. The vault's DNS record is kept during the retention interval, soft-delete can't be turned off once it's on, and recovery undoes the deletion rather than leaving the vault read-only.

questions.prompt: A team switches an existing vault from access policies to the Azure RBAC permission model, and its apps get 403 errors at once. What happened?

options.text: The switch voided the old permissions, and no matching roles had been assigned
Apps must move from azure-keyvault-secrets to an RBAC-specific client library
Role assignments made after a permission model switch take 24 hours to apply
The RBAC model covers keys and certificates, while secrets still need policies

questions.explanation: Setting the Azure RBAC permission model invalidates the vault's access policies, so apps fail until each identity holds an equivalent data-plane role, such as one of the Key Vault secrets roles. The 403s start at the switch itself, before any role exists, so no propagation delay explains them, and the vault guide expects a role assigned directly to an identity to apply within several minutes. The same azure-keyvault-secrets client works under either model, and Azure RBAC has built-in roles for secrets as well as keys and certificates.

questions.prompt: Woodgrove automates its rotation with a function triggered by the SecretNearExpiry event, and each new version the function writes gets an expiration date a fixed number of days after it's created. To meet the security team's rotation cycle, how many days after creation should each new version expire? Answer in days. Enter a number.
questions.explanation: Key Vault raises SecretNearExpiry 30 days before the current version's expiration date, and the function rotates when that event arrives. A version that expires 90 days after creation therefore triggers the next rotation on day 60, which matches the 60-day cycle; Learn's two-key tutorial shows the same arithmetic, where a 60-day expiry makes the event fire every 30 days.

questions.prompt: One of Margie's Travel's partner import tools must load the API keys of all partners from Key Vault when it starts, using azure-keyvault-secrets. Which approach returns the key values and meets the requirements?

options.text: Call list_properties_of_secrets and read .value from each returned item
List the secrets' properties, then call get_secret for each name
Call get_secret once with the vault URL, which returns every secret
Have the CI pipeline copy each partner key into the tool's app settings

questions.explanation: list_properties_of_secrets returns each secret's name and metadata but never its value, so the tool reads the values with get_secret, one name at a time, under its own identity. Copying the keys into app settings breaks the rule that secret values never appear there, and get_secret retrieves one named secret rather than the whole vault.

questions.prompt: A function rotates a SQL login password stored in Key Vault. For a short time after each rotation, apps that fetch the secret fail to sign in, and then they recover with no change. What explains this?

options.text: Key Vault holds the new password before the server accepts it
Each new secret version needs its own vault role assignment for the apps
The function wrote the new password version without an expiration date
Event Grid delivered the event to the apps before it reached the server

questions.explanation: Learn's single-credential tutorial warns that there can be a lag between creating the new secret version and updating the server, and that during that window the secret in Key Vault can't authenticate. Roles are assigned at vault or secret scope, not per version, the expiry date only schedules the next event, and the apps aren't Event Grid subscribers; a two-credential design avoids the gap because the regenerated key isn't in use yet.

questions.prompt: An inventory tool's identity holds Key Vault Reader on a vault that uses the access policy permission model, and it can't list the vault's secrets with their tags and expiration dates. The vault's permission model must stay as it is. What should you do?

options.text: Assign Key Vault Reader at subscription scope, above the vault's policy
Add an access policy that grants the tool's identity the Get secret permission
Add an access policy that grants the tool's identity the List secret permission
Also assign the tool's identity Key Vault Secrets User for secret access

questions.explanation: Under the access policy model, data-plane access comes from access policies, which grant secret permissions such as get and list to a security principal, for example with az keyvault set-policy and --secret-permissions; listing secrets and their metadata needs list, not get. Learn's role table says the Key Vault data roles, Reader and Secrets User included, only work for vaults that use the Azure RBAC permission model, so neither another role nor a wider scope helps. Get reads a secret's value by name but doesn't enumerate the vault's secrets, which is the list operation.

questions.prompt: An administrator must switch an existing vault from access policies to the Azure RBAC permission model in the Azure portal while holding a single built-in role on it. Which role is enough on its own?

options.text: User Access Administrator
Owner
Key Vault Data Access Administrator
Key Vault Administrator

questions.explanation: Changing the permission model needs unrestricted Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write, which Owner and User Access Administrator have; User Access Administrator also needs Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/write, for example from Key Vault Contributor, so it isn't enough alone. Learn says the restricted Key Vault Data Access Administrator can't change the model, and Key Vault Administrator performs data-plane operations without managing role assignments.

questions.prompt: A platform lead must be able to give new apps the Key Vault Secrets User role on a team's vault. They must have no way to grant broader roles such as Owner. Which built-in role fits?

options.text: Key Vault Certificates Officer
Key Vault Administrator
Key Vault Data Access Administrator
User Access Administrator

questions.explanation: Key Vault Data Access Administrator manages access by adding or removing assignments of the Key Vault data roles, such as Secrets User, and includes an ABAC condition that constrains which roles it can assign. User Access Administrator can assign any role, Key Vault Administrator performs data-plane operations but can't manage role assignments, and Certificates Officer manages certificates, not access.

questions.prompt: A batch job starts 200 replicas at once, and each replica reads the same three secrets from Key Vault at start-up. The vault throttles them. Which change follows Learn's guidance for this pattern?

options.text: Retry each 429 response at once so that the replicas start on time
Move all apps and regions onto one shared vault so that its request limit is pooled
Have one component read the secrets and hand them to the replicas in memory
Cache the secrets in each replica's memory after its first read

questions.explanation: For many nodes that need the same secrets, Learn suggests a fan-out pattern in which one entity reads from Key Vault and passes the values to the nodes, caching them only in memory. A per-replica cache doesn't help because each replica reads only once, at start-up. Learn recommends separate vaults per app and region rather than one pooled vault, and immediate retries add to the load that caused the throttling.

questions.prompt: A SaaS app keeps an API token for each of its 50,000 customers and reads those tokens at a high rate. Following Learn's Key Vault throttling guidance, where should the customers' tokens be stored?

options.text: In Key Vault, as one secret per customer in a single shared vault
In the app's settings, because Key Vault limits don't suit runtime reads
In Key Vault, with a separate vault for each customer's token
In an encrypted database or storage account, keeping only its key in Key Vault

questions.explanation: Learn says Key Vault is designed for your own services' secrets, and that for customers' secrets, especially in high-throughput scenarios, you should put them in a database or storage account with encryption and store just the primary key in Key Vault. A single vault concentrates the load the guidance warns about, a vault per customer isn't what Learn suggests, and app settings leave the tokens outside any secret store.

questions.prompt: A vault has soft-delete on and purge protection off. Which TWO statements are true? Select TWO.

options.text: A deleted vault's name can be reused at once in another resource group
Purging a deleted secret needs a purge permission, such as Key Vault Purge Operator
Deleted secrets are kept for 30 days unless a longer period was chosen
Soft-delete can be turned off again because purge protection is off
If the vault itself is deleted, its DNS record is kept during the retention period

questions.explanation: Permanently deleting a soft-deleted object requires the purge permission, for example through the Key Vault Purge Operator role, and the vault's DNS record is retained along with its data during the retention interval. Soft-delete can't be disabled once it's on, the default retention is 90 days, and a soft-deleted vault's name can't be reused until the retention period ends.

questions.prompt: An asyncio web service reads secrets with azure-keyvault-secrets. Which TWO things does the README say it needs? Select TWO.

options.text: SecretClient from azure.keyvault.secrets.aio with a credential from azure.identity.aio
async_mode=True passed to the SecretClient from azure.keyvault.secrets
get_secret_async calls on the synchronous SecretClient
A separate azure-keyvault-secrets-async package from PyPI
An async transport such as aiohttp, installed alongside the package

questions.explanation: The async APIs live in the aio modules of both packages, so the service imports SecretClient from azure.keyvault.secrets.aio and an async credential from azure.identity.aio, and the README says an async transport such as aiohttp must be installed first. There is no async_mode switch, no separate async package and no _async variant of the synchronous methods; the async clients should also be closed or used as async context managers.

questions.prompt: Complete the Python handler that an Event Grid-triggered rotation function runs for a Key Vault SecretNearExpiry event in the Event Grid schema.

slots.text: Name of the secret: data["____"]

options.text: VaultName
ObjectType
ObjectName

slots.text: Read the one that triggered the event: client.get_secret(name, data["____"])

options.text: Version
Id
NBF

slots.text: data["EXP"] holds the expiration date as

options.text: days left until expiry
seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC
an ISO 8601 date string

questions.explanation: The event's data object names the secret in ObjectName and the vault in VaultName, while ObjectType holds the kind of object, such as Secret. Version identifies the version that triggered the event and is what get_secret takes as its version argument; Id is the full object URI and NBF the not-before date. Both NBF and EXP are numbers of seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z.

questions.prompt: Complete the az keyvault secret set call that stores a storage account key for Learn's two-key rotation function.

slots.text: Record which of the account's keys this version holds: --tags ____

options.text: "ProviderAddress=key1"
"CredentialId=key1"
"ValidityPeriodDays=key1"

slots.text: Tell the function which storage account to regenerate the key in: --tags ____

options.text: "ProviderAddress=<storage account resource ID>"
"CredentialId=<storage account resource ID>"
"VaultName=<storage account resource ID>"

slots.text: Set the date that SecretNearExpiry counts back from: ____ $tomorrowDate

options.text: --expires
--not-before
--disabled

questions.explanation: The rotation function reads its inputs from the secret's tags: CredentialId says which key (key1 or key2) the version holds, ProviderAddress gives the storage account's resource ID, and ValidityPeriodDays sets the lifetime of the next version. --expires sets the expiration date that the near-expiry event is raised 30 days before, whereas --not-before sets when the version becomes usable and --disabled only creates the version in a disabled state.

questions.prompt: For each statement about Learn's Key Vault throttling guidance, select Yes if it's true or No if it isn't.

options.text: Yes
No

slots.text: Five apps that each run in two regions should use 10 vaults, one per app and region
Requests that fail with HTTP 429 count toward the throttle limits
Using Microsoft Entra authentication where the target service supports it reduces load on Key Vault
Public-key operations such as signature verification should be sent to Key Vault every time

questions.explanation: Learn recommends a separate vault for each security or availability domain, with its example of five apps in two regions using 10 vaults, and it says failed 429 requests don't count toward the tracked limits. Authenticating to a service directly with Microsoft Entra ID removes the secret lookup altogether, and public-key operations should be done locally with cached public key material.

questions.prompt: Put the steps in order to test Learn's single-credential rotation function for a SQL Server password once it's deployed.

options.text: The function rotates the password and records it as a new version
Open the test web app to confirm that it still connects to the database
Set the secret with the server's tags and an expiration date of tomorrow
Key Vault publishes SecretNearExpiry, within about 15 minutes

questions.explanation: The tutorial sets the secret's expiration to tomorrow so that rotation starts at once, and a short expiry publishes SecretNearExpiry within 15 minutes. That event triggers the function, which creates the new secret version and updates SQL Server. The test web app, which reads the secret and tests the connection, can only confirm the result afterwards.

questions.prompt: A team deploys a new vault with an ARM template that uses API version 2026-02-01 and contains access policies but no permission-model property. Apps then get 403 errors. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: That API version removed the access policy permission model entirely
Access policies need a separate deployment after the new vault exists
New vaults reject all data-plane calls until purge protection is on
Azure RBAC is the default permission model for new vaults from that version

questions.explanation: Starting with API version 2026-02-01, Azure RBAC is the default access control model for newly created vaults, so access policies in the template don't authorize anything and the apps need Key Vault data roles instead. The access policy model remains available as a legacy option, and Learn's guidance on the change involves neither a second deployment nor purge protection.

questions.prompt: A Python app must use unlabelled settings by default, with prod-labelled values overriding them where both exist. How should it pass its two SettingSelector objects to load()?

options.text: The selector for the prod label first, then the unlabelled selector
The unlabelled selector first, then the selector for the prod label
One selector whose label filter matches any label
One selector whose label filter is set to prod

questions.explanation: Selectors load in the order they're listed, and when two return the same key the later one wins, so the prod selector has to come after the unlabelled one. Reversing them lets the unlabelled values overwrite prod, a filter that matches any label also pulls in other environments' variants, and a prod filter on its own drops the settings that exist without a label.

questions.prompt: A Python app's settings, loaded with azure-appconfiguration-provider, include Key Vault references. Which TWO load() arguments can each, used on its own, let the provider resolve them? Each correct answer is a complete solution. Select TWO.

options.text: refresh_on=[WatchKey("Sentinel")]
replica_discovery_enabled=False
keyvault_credential=credential
startup_timeout=300
keyvault_client_configs={kv_uri: {"credential": credential}}

questions.explanation: keyvault_credential gives the provider one credential for every vault that the references point to, and keyvault_client_configs maps each vault URI to its own client settings when vaults need different credentials. Without one of them, or a secret resolver, the provider has no way to read the secrets; startup_timeout, replica discovery and refresh_on control start-up retries, failover and reloads.

questions.prompt: A Python API reads settings from App Configuration through Microsoft Entra ID and doesn't change them. Which built-in role gives it what it needs with the smallest set of rights?

options.text: App Configuration Reader
App Configuration Data Reader
App Configuration Contributor
App Configuration Data Owner

questions.explanation: App Configuration Data Reader grants read access to the store's key-values over Microsoft Entra ID and nothing on the resource itself. App Configuration Reader is a control-plane role that sees the resource but not its data, Data Owner adds write and delete, and Contributor manages the resource and can read its access keys, which is far more than a reader needs.

questions.prompt: Put the steps in order to roll out new search settings to running Python apps that watch a sentinel key.

options.text: After the sentinel changes, a running app calls refresh() once its refresh interval has passed
Update the value of the Search:Sentinel key
The provider sees the changed sentinel and reloads all selected keys
Update the Search:TopK and Search:MinScore values in the store

questions.explanation: The apps watch the sentinel alone, so it's updated after the real settings to make each app reload a complete, consistent set. The provider checks the watched key when the app calls refresh() and the refresh interval has elapsed (earlier calls return at once), and a detected change reloads every selected key in one go.

questions.prompt: Complete the load() call that a Python reports worker uses for keys such as Reports:Timeout and Reports:Limits.

slots.text: selects=[SettingSelector(key_filter=____)]  # keys that start with Reports:

options.text: "Reports:*"
"Reports:Timeout"

slots.text: Read config["Timeout"] instead of config["Reports:Timeout"]: ____=["Reports:"]

options.text: trim_prefixes
refresh_on
tag_filters

slots.text: Reports:Limits has content type application/json and value {"rows": 500}, so config["Limits"] is

options.text: a ConfigurationSetting whose .value holds the JSON
a dict, and config["Limits"]["rows"] is 500
a str that has to go through json.loads first

questions.explanation: A trailing asterisk matches every key that begins with the prefix, while a full name such as Reports:Timeout matches that one key and * alone loads the whole store. trim_prefixes strips the listed prefixes from loaded key names, whereas tag_filters selects key-values by tag and refresh_on names watch keys. The provider deserializes key-values that have a JSON content type into Python objects, so the value arrives as a dict.

questions.prompt: Which statement about keys in an App Configuration store is true?

options.text: A key-value and its attributes can total up to 1 MB
app1 and App1 are two different keys
A key name can use any Unicode character, % included
The store splits keys on : to enforce a hierarchy

questions.explanation: Keys are case-sensitive Unicode strings, so app1 and App1 are distinct, though Learn advises against telling keys apart by case. The % character isn't allowed in key names, a key-value with all its attributes is limited to 10 KB, and App Configuration treats each key as a whole without parsing delimiters.

questions.prompt: Fabrikam's Python copilot API calls load() with its endpoint and credential and hands the result to FeatureManager, but the manager can't find an unlabelled flag that is on in the store. What should change?

options.text: Pass feature_flag_enabled=True when calling load()
Add the flag to refresh_on as a WatchKey
Register a custom feature filter named after the flag
Lower refresh_interval so that the flag arrives sooner

questions.explanation: The provider loads no feature flags unless feature_flag_enabled is True; with it, unlabelled flags land in the feature_management section that FeatureManager reads. Watch keys and the refresh interval decide when data that was already loaded is reloaded, and feature filters evaluate flags that have been loaded, so none of them brings the missing flag in.

questions.prompt: A Python API loads its settings with a sentinel watch key, resolves a Key Vault reference through the App Configuration provider and calls refresh() on each request. After the password is rotated in Key Vault, the API keeps the old value, and the store itself hasn't changed. What should you add to load()?

options.text: refresh_interval=5
secret_refresh_interval=3600
refresh_enabled=True, so that all loaded keys are watched
refresh_on=[WatchKey("Payments:DbPassword")]

questions.explanation: Refresh is already on because the API watches a sentinel, and secret_refresh_interval makes the provider fetch resolved secrets from Key Vault again on refresh() once that interval has passed, even when nothing in the store changed. The reference itself still holds the same URI after a rotation, so watching it, monitoring all loaded keys or checking the store more often can't detect a change.

questions.prompt: Alpine Ski House's Flask app loads its settings with a sentinel watch key, copies them into app.config once at start-up and calls refresh() on the provider in each route. After the team changes the threshold and then the sentinel, the routes still read the old value from app.config. What should be added?

options.text: feature_flag_refresh_enabled=True, so that app.config tracks every key
A shorter refresh_interval, so that each refresh() checks the sentinel sooner
A second WatchKey on the provider for the threshold key
An on_refresh_success callback that runs app.config.update with the provider

questions.explanation: refresh() updates the provider object, but app.config still holds the copy made at start-up. Learn's Flask sample passes on_refresh_success to load() and calls app.config.update with the provider in it, and the callback runs only when a change is detected. A shorter interval or another watch key changes when the provider reloads, not the stale copy, and feature_flag_refresh_enabled concerns feature flags.

questions.prompt: A Python worker must pick up any change to the key-values it loaded, and the team doesn't want to maintain a sentinel key. The worker calls refresh() before each job. Which load() setting meets this?

options.text: secret_refresh_interval=60
replica_discovery_enabled=True
feature_flag_refresh_enabled=True
refresh_enabled=True with no refresh_on

questions.explanation: With refresh_enabled set to True and no refresh_on, the provider monitors all loaded key-values for changes, and refresh() reloads them once the refresh interval has passed; refresh_on narrows monitoring to watch keys. secret_refresh_interval refetches Key Vault secrets, feature_flag_refresh_enabled covers feature flags, and replica discovery only finds geo-replicas for failover.

questions.prompt: A SettingSelector uses key filter * and label filter * with tag filters for env=prod and region=us. Which key-values does it load?

options.text: Those tagged env=prod, with region=us applied as a fallback
Every key-value, using the tags only to order the results
Those tagged with either env=prod or region=us
Only those tagged with both env=prod and region=us

questions.explanation: A key-value is loaded only if it has all of the tags and values named in the tag filters, so the filters combine like AND. They don't act as alternatives, ordering hints or fallbacks; note also that *, the comma and the backslash are reserved in tag filters and need a backslash escape.

questions.prompt: load() uses trim_prefixes=["App1/"] and a configuration_mapper that changes the value when setting.key == "message". The store's key is App1/message, and its value is never changed. Why?

options.text: trim_prefixes drops App1/message from the result, since it has the prefix
A mapper has to return a new setting instead of editing the one passed in
Mappers apply only to key-values that have a JSON content type
The mapper runs before key trimming, so it compares against App1/message

questions.explanation: The provider calls the mapper for each loaded setting before key trimming is applied, so the mapper sees App1/message and must compare against the original key. Mappers run for every setting whatever its content type, trim_prefixes shortens key names rather than removing keys, and Learn's sample edits the setting in place.

questions.prompt: A Python API calls load() with feature_flag_enabled=True and a sentinel in refresh_on, and calls refresh() on each request. Turning a flag off in the store changes nothing in the running API, even after the sentinel is updated. What should be added to load()?

options.text: feature_flag_refresh_enabled=True
refresh_interval=5, so that the sentinel is checked sooner
feature_flag_selectors that select the flags with no label
refresh_enabled=True, alongside the sentinel in refresh_on

questions.explanation: Feature flags are refreshed only when feature_flag_refresh_enabled is True; then every loaded flag is monitored, and refresh() updates flags and settings independently, so a sentinel change never reloads flags. refresh_on already turns on refresh for settings, unlabelled flags are loaded by default, and a shorter interval only checks the sentinel more often.

questions.prompt: Minutes after a new managed identity is given App Configuration Data Reader on a store, the app's first load() calls return 403, and later calls succeed with no change. What explains this?

options.text: Role assignments can take up to 15 minutes to propagate
The provider retries with a connection string minutes after a failure
A new identity first needs App Configuration Reader on the store
Data Reader works only once the store's access keys are enabled

questions.explanation: Learn says to allow up to 15 minutes after a role assignment before the identity can access the store's data, and the dynamic configuration tutorial repeats the advice to wait for propagation. Data Reader is an Entra ID data-plane role that needs no access keys, the provider doesn't switch credentials, and the control-plane App Configuration Reader role grants no data access.

questions.prompt: Security wants principals that hold App Configuration Contributor on a store to have no way to read or change its key-values. Which control does Learn point to?

options.text: Assigning App Configuration Reader to them alongside Contributor
Removing App Configuration Data Reader from those principals
An Azure Policy that enforces disabled access key authentication
Moving the store's secret values into Key Vault references

questions.explanation: App Configuration Contributor can't read data through Microsoft Entra ID, but it can enable access key authentication and read the access keys, and with a key it can read and modify key-values. Learn's answer is Azure Policy that enforces disabled access key authentication. Removing or adding Entra data or reader roles doesn't touch the key path, and Key Vault references protect only secrets, not other key-values.

questions.prompt: Which TWO statements about loading an App Configuration snapshot with the Python provider are true? Select TWO.

options.text: A selector that sets snapshot_name can't also set key_filter, label_filter or tag_filters
A snapshot's settings are loaded only when feature_flag_enabled is True
Snapshot selectors work with every provider version from 1.0 onward
Only snapshots created with composition type Key can be loaded
Snapshots created with composition type Key_Label load as well, with their labels kept

questions.explanation: A SettingSelector with snapshot_name loads every setting in that snapshot, and snapshot_name can't be combined with key, label or tag filters. The provider can load only snapshots whose composition type is Key, snapshot support starts with version 2.3.0, and loading key-values from a snapshot doesn't depend on feature_flag_enabled.

questions.prompt: A feature flag lists a Microsoft.TimeWindow filter and a Microsoft.Targeting filter and sets no requirement_type. Which TWO statements are true? Select TWO.

options.text: The flag is on whenever either filter evaluates to true
With requirement_type All and its filters removed, the flag is always on
A filter that isn't registered with FeatureManager is skipped
Both filters have to pass, because All is the default requirement type
With requirement_type set to All, it's on just for the audience during the window

questions.explanation: requirement_type defaults to Any, so the filters are traversed until one enables the feature. With All, every filter must evaluate to true, so the flag is on for the targeted audience inside the window, and an All flag with no filters is disabled. A filter that the flag names but FeatureManager hasn't registered raises ValueError when the flag is evaluated.

questions.prompt: For each statement about refresh in azure-appconfiguration-provider, select Yes if it's true or No if it isn't.

options.text: No
Yes

slots.text: If a refresh() call fails, the app keeps using the configuration it already has
on_refresh_success runs after every refresh() call that reaches the store
A changed feature flag also triggers a reload of the configuration settings
refresh() returns without contacting the store until the refresh interval has passed

questions.explanation: A failed refresh leaves the cached configuration in place, and another attempt is made after the next interval. on_refresh_success is called only when a change is detected and no error occurs. Flag refresh and settings refresh are independent, so a flag change doesn't reload settings, and refresh() is a no-op before the interval elapses.

questions.prompt: For each statement about the built-in feature filters in the Python featuremanagement library, select Yes if it's true or No if it isn't.

options.text: Yes
No

slots.text: A Microsoft.TimeWindow filter with only an End value keeps the feature on until that time
A recurring time window needs both a Start and an End value
A 25-hour time window can recur every day
A user named in an audience's Users stays included when an Exclusion lists a group they're in

questions.explanation: With only End, the feature is on until that time, and recurrence requires Start and End, whose difference sets the length of each window. A window can't be longer than how often it recurs, so 25 hours can't repeat daily. In a targeting audience, exclusions take priority over the rest of the filter.

questions.prompt: Complete the Microsoft.Targeting audience for a Beta feature flag defined for the Python featuremanagement library.

slots.text: Always on for Jeff and Alicia: "____": ["Jeff", "Alicia"]

options.text: Groups
Users
Exclusion

slots.text: Half of the Ring1 group: "Groups": [{"Name": "Ring1", "____": 50}]

options.text: DefaultRolloutPercentage
Value
RolloutPercentage

slots.text: One in five of all other users: "____": 20

options.text: GroupRolloutPercentage
DefaultRolloutPercentage
RolloutPercentage

questions.explanation: Users lists people who always get the feature, while Exclusion removes users and groups and takes priority. Each entry under Groups sets RolloutPercentage, the share of that group's members included, and DefaultRolloutPercentage sets the share of the whole user base. Value belongs to a percentage-style filter's parameters, not to a targeting audience.

questions.prompt: Put in order the checks that FeatureManager makes to choose a variant for a user when a variant feature flag is enabled.

options.text: The group allocation, which matches the user's groups
The user allocation, which lists variants for named users
default_when_enabled, used when no allocation matched
The percentile allocation, based on the user's calculated percentage

questions.explanation: For an enabled flag, the feature manager checks the user, group and percentile allocations in that order and assigns the first variant that matches. If none matches, the user gets the default_when_enabled variant; default_when_disabled applies only while the flag is disabled.

questions.prompt: Which setup does Microsoft Learn now recommend for sending a new Python service's telemetry to Application Insights?

options.text: Initialize the Microsoft distro and the Azure Monitor distro together at start-up
Install azure-monitor-query and create a LogsQueryClient when the service starts
Install microsoft-opentelemetry and call use_microsoft_opentelemetry(enable_azure_monitor=True)
Install opentelemetry-exporter-otlp and point its span exporter at the connection string

questions.explanation: For new .NET, Node.js and Python apps, Learn now points to the Microsoft OpenTelemetry Distro, whose Python package microsoft-opentelemetry exports to Azure Monitor once use_microsoft_opentelemetry is called with enable_azure_monitor=True. azure-monitor-query reads data back out of a workspace, the OTLP exporter sends to an OTLP collector and isn't officially supported by Microsoft, and Learn says not to initialize the two distros in one app.

questions.prompt: docs-api and docs-worker both use microsoft-opentelemetry and send to one Application Insights resource, yet Application Map shows them as a single node. What should Contoso change?

options.text: Give docs-worker a lower sampling ratio than docs-api
Add a span processor that sets a role attribute on each span
Give docs-api and docs-worker different OTEL_SERVICE_NAME values
Give docs-worker its own logger_name in use_microsoft_opentelemetry

questions.explanation: Application Map names each node after the cloud role name, which the distro builds from the service.namespace and service.name resource attributes, and OTEL_SERVICE_NAME sets service.name; Learn requires distinct cloud role names when several services share one resource. Span attributes become custom properties rather than the role name, sampling changes how much is kept, and logger_name chooses which Python logger's records are collected.

questions.prompt: A Python worker wraps each queue job in tracer.start_as_current_span from the opentelemetry API, and the jobs show up as InProc dependencies instead of requests. What should you change?

options.text: Set a span attribute named type to the value Request
Start the span with kind=SpanKind.SERVER
Set OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER to always_on before the distro starts
Start the span with record_exception=False

questions.explanation: A custom span lands in the dependencies table as InProc by default, and Learn recommends kind=SpanKind.SERVER for a background job that autoinstrumentation doesn't capture, so that it's recorded as a request. record_exception controls whether exceptions raised in the block are recorded, a span attribute becomes a custom property without changing the telemetry type, and the sampler decides how many traces are kept.

questions.prompt: Match each call in a Python app that uses microsoft-opentelemetry, where logger is the logger named in logger_name, to the Application Insights telemetry type it produces.

options.text: Metric
Event
Page view
Trace
Request
Exception

slots.text: logger.warning("Checkout failed", extra={"microsoft.custom_event.name": "checkout"})
meter.create_histogram("rerank_ms").record(42.0, {"model": "small"})
logger.info("Cache warmed", extra={"tenant": tenant_id})
span.record_exception(ex)

questions.explanation: A log record whose extra holds microsoft.custom_event.name becomes an event in customEvents, while ordinary records from the collected logger become traces with the extra keys as custom dimensions. A histogram from the OpenTelemetry metrics API produces a metric, and record_exception attaches an exception to the current span. None of these calls creates a request or a page view, and Learn lists no Python page-view API for the distro.

questions.prompt: A new Python service initializes microsoft-opentelemetry and sets no sampler. How are its traces sampled?

options.text: Rate-limited sampling of about five traces per second
Ingestion sampling applied by the Application Insights resource
Fixed-percentage sampling that keeps about 5 percent of traces
Fixed-percentage sampling that keeps all traces

questions.explanation: The Microsoft OpenTelemetry Distro for Python defaults to the rate-limited sampler at five traces per second for Azure Monitor export. Five percent is the starting rate that Learn suggests if you choose fixed-percentage sampling yourself, keeping all traces needs an explicit setting, and ingestion sampling is set on the resource in the portal and stays off until someone picks a percentage there.

questions.prompt: A Python service calls configure_azure_monitor(connection_string=conn_a) from azure-monitor-opentelemetry, and its container also sets APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING to conn_b. Where does its telemetry go?

options.text: To both, with one copy of the telemetry for each string
Nowhere, since the distro rejects two conflicting settings
To conn_a, since passed-in arguments win over environment variables
To conn_b, since environment variables win over code arguments

questions.explanation: The azure-monitor-opentelemetry README says that every argument passed to configure_azure_monitor takes priority over the related environment variable, so the explicit connection_string decides where telemetry goes. The environment variable is read only when no connection string is passed, the distro exports to a single connection string, and nothing fails on the overlap; sampling is the documented exception, where environment variables win over distro options.

questions.prompt: A Python service that uses microsoft-opentelemetry records processed jobs with a Counter and queue depth with an observable gauge. Which TWO Metrics Explorer aggregations does Learn recommend for them? Select TWO.

options.text: Average for the processed-jobs counter
Sum for the processed-jobs counter
Max for the processed-jobs counter
Average for the queue-depth gauge
Sum for the queue-depth gauge

questions.explanation: Learn pairs each OpenTelemetry instrument with an Azure Monitor aggregation: a Counter adds up increments, so Sum is its meaningful view, and an asynchronous (observable) gauge reports a current level, so Average fits it. Summing gauge readings, or averaging or taking the maximum of counter values, gives numbers that Learn calls not meaningful in most cases.

questions.prompt: A Python API and two Python workers use microsoft-opentelemetry with its fixed-percentage Application Insights sampler, and their traces often look incomplete; the API samples 20 percent, the workers 50 percent, and the resource adds ingestion sampling. Which TWO changes reduce the broken traces? Select TWO.

options.text: Let each worker follow the sampled flag that the API's sampler propagates
Remove the resource-level sampling and sample in each service instead
Use a lower sampling rate for dependencies than for requests
Give the API and both workers the same sampler and the same rate
Set a daily cap on the Application Insights resource

questions.explanation: The Application Insights sampler decides independently in each service from a hash of the trace ID, so traces stay whole when all components use the same sampler and rate, and sampling at the source keeps complete traces where ingestion sampling drops items regardless of the trace they belong to. This sampler decides at the end of each span, after the downstream calls, so the flag the API propagates is incomplete and the workers can't rely on it; it also applies one rate to all telemetry types in a trace, and a daily cap creates gaps instead of consistent sampling.

questions.prompt: A Python service that uses microsoft-opentelemetry sets OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL to 15000 so that its custom metrics update faster in Azure Monitor Metrics. How often does Azure Monitor Metrics process those metrics? Answer in seconds. Enter a number.
questions.explanation: OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL, in milliseconds with a default of 60000, sets how often the SDK sends metrics, but Azure Monitor Metrics ingests custom metrics at a fixed 60-second interval and buffers anything sent more often. A shorter interval therefore doesn't speed up Metrics, and in Log Analytics, which records metrics at the interval they're sent, it can raise cost.

questions.prompt: recommend-api calls configure_azure_monitor from azure-monitor-opentelemetry with instrumentation_options={"azure_sdk": {"enabled": False}} to cut noise. In the end-to-end transaction view, its requests show a long gap with no child calls, although each one queries article-vectors. What should Lucerne change?

options.text: Set OTEL_SERVICE_NAME to recommend-api in the Azure container app's environment
Start each request's span with kind=SpanKind.SERVER so child calls attach
Raise OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG on recommend-api so that every request's trace is kept in full
Turn Azure Core Tracing back on, which tracks Cosmos DB client calls as dependencies

questions.explanation: azure_sdk is the bundled Azure Core Tracing instrumentation, on by default, and it traces calls made through Azure SDK clients such as the Cosmos DB client, so turning it off removes those dependencies. Learn's FAQ says time a transaction doesn't explain is time not covered by a tracked dependency. A SERVER span kind decides the requests table, the service name sets the map node, and sampling can't add spans that were never created.

questions.prompt: The speech pipeline adds W3C traceparent and tracestate application properties to each transcripts message. insight-worker wraps the work for each message in tracer.start_as_current_span, yet every call's trace starts afresh at the worker. What should insight-worker do?

options.text: Pass extract() of the message's trace properties as the span's context
Copy the speech pipeline's OTEL_SERVICE_NAME into the message properties
Start the span for each message with kind=SpanKind.SERVER
Set OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER to parentbased_always_on so the trace follows

questions.explanation: A span without a parent context starts a new trace. opentelemetry.propagate.extract turns a carrier that holds traceparent and tracestate into a context, and Learn's Functions sample passes context=extract(carrier) to start_as_current_span for the same kind of correlation. A SERVER kind changes the table, not the parent, a shared service name merges map nodes, and a parent-based sampler needs a parent the span still wouldn't have.

questions.prompt: A Python service passes azure_monitor_connection_string to use_microsoft_opentelemetry in its code. For production, where does Learn recommend that the connection string comes from?

options.text: An instrumentation key passed in place of the connection string
The APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING environment variable
An applicationinsights.json file placed beside the app's code
A constants module that the service imports at start-up

questions.explanation: Learn recommends setting the connection string in code only for local development and test, and an environment variable for production in every language. The applicationinsights.json file is a Java-only option, a constants module is still code, and Learn points to connection strings rather than instrumentation keys.

questions.prompt: A Python service samples 20 percent of its traces with the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro sampler, and its Application Insights resource also has ingestion sampling set to keep 50 percent. Roughly what share of the service's traces is stored? Answer in percent. Enter a number.
questions.explanation: Ingestion sampling only drops part of what reaches the service, so with both in place the effective rate is multiplicative: 20 percent of 50 percent is about 10 percent. The classic SDK rule that ingestion sampling skips telemetry the SDK has already sampled doesn't apply to the OpenTelemetry sampler. Learn uses this same example and recommends sampling at the source, keeping ingestion sampling as a fallback.

questions.prompt: A team moves a Python service from azure-monitor-opentelemetry to microsoft-opentelemetry and wants to keep sampling about 10 percent of traces, as sampling_ratio=0.1 did before. What should it do?

options.text: Set OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER to microsoft.fixed_percentage with an ARG of 0.1
Pass sampling_ratio=0.1 to use_microsoft_opentelemetry
Set OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER to microsoft.rate_limited with an ARG of 0.1
Put the percentage in a sampling section of a configuration file

questions.explanation: For the Microsoft distro, Learn configures Python sampling through OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER and OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG, set before the distro starts, and says not to carry over the older distro's sampling_ratio and traces_per_second arguments. Python doesn't support sampling settings in a configuration file, and microsoft.rate_limited would treat 0.1 as traces per second, not as a ratio.

questions.prompt: A Python service uses microsoft-opentelemetry with fixed-percentage sampling at 10 percent, yet AppTraces holds log records for every request, including requests whose traces weren't kept. What change aligns the logs with the sampled traces while keeping its 10 percent trace sampling?

options.text: Add ingestion sampling at 10 percent on the Application Insights resource
Write the log records outside any active span so that they're sampled
Switch microsoft-opentelemetry to always_on so every trace and log is kept
Pass enable_trace_based_sampling_for_logs=True to use_microsoft_opentelemetry

questions.explanation: Trace-based sampling for logs drops log records that carry a valid span ID from an unsampled trace, and the Python Microsoft distro leaves it off by default, so it has to be enabled. always_on abandons the 10 percent trace sampling instead of reducing the logs, records without trace context aren't affected at all, and ingestion sampling drops items without regard to the trace they belong to.

questions.prompt: A Python service calls use_microsoft_opentelemetry(enable_azure_monitor=True, logger_name="app") and logs checkout events with logging.getLogger("checkout").info(..., extra={"microsoft.custom_event.name": "checkout"}). No rows appear in customEvents. What should change?

options.text: Log the events at WARNING level, because INFO records are dropped
Rename the extra key to microsoft.custom_event.type
Record them as attributes on the span that's active for the logger
Log the events through the logger named in logger_name

questions.explanation: The distro collects log records only from the logger named in logger_name, which also keeps the SDK's own logs out, so records from another logger never reach customEvents. Learn's sample sends an event at info level, span attributes become custom properties rather than events, and microsoft.custom_event.name is the documented key.

questions.prompt: A Python service uses microsoft-opentelemetry, and its network path to Application Insights fails for six hours. Which TWO statements are true? Select TWO.

options.text: azure_monitor_exporter_disable_offline_storage=True would turn that local storage off
When the storage limit is reached, the oldest telemetry is kept first
The telemetry waits in memory and is lost if the process restarts meanwhile
Retries stop after two hours, and telemetry from later on is dropped
The exporter stores the telemetry locally and retries sending it for up to 48 hours

questions.explanation: Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry-based offerings cache telemetry on disk while disconnected and retry for up to 48 hours, and the Python option azure_monitor_exporter_disable_offline_storage turns that off. When time or file-size limits force drops, recent events are prioritized over old ones, and nothing limits the retries to two hours.

questions.prompt: A Python service uses microsoft-opentelemetry and adds SQLAlchemy tracing with SQLAlchemyInstrumentor().instrument(engine=engine). What does Learn say about community instrumentation libraries like this one?

options.text: They're supported once their package reaches a stable release
Microsoft doesn't support them or guarantee their quality
They take over from the distro's own instrumentation of the same library
They're bundled in Microsoft's azure-monitor-opentelemetry for production use

questions.explanation: Learn's caution for community instrumentation libraries is that Microsoft doesn't support or guarantee their quality, and that some are based on experimental OpenTelemetry specifications and might break later; you can suggest one for the distro in the feedback community. Neither distro bundles SQLAlchemy, and Learn says not to instrument by hand a library that the distro already instruments, because duplicate instrumentation isn't supported.

questions.prompt: A Python API returns 404 for unknown product IDs, and the Failures view counts those requests as failed. The team wants 404 responses counted as successful while 5xx responses stay failures. What does Learn show for this?

options.text: Setting enduser.id on every request span that returns 404
A custom event named after the route for each 404 response
A span processor whose on_end sets 4xx SERVER spans to an OK status
A span processor whose on_start sets the status code attribute to 200

questions.explanation: Learn's processor checks SERVER spans in on_end, reads the HTTP status code attribute and sets a status of OK for 4xx codes, optionally keeping some, such as 429, as failures. In on_start the response doesn't exist yet, enduser.id only records the user, and an extra custom event leaves the request marked failed.

questions.prompt: For Python, when does Learn recommend the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Exporter instead of the Microsoft OpenTelemetry Distro?

options.text: When the same application also contains a Java component
When telemetry has to be sent from users' web browsers
For each new Python service that sends telemetry to Application Insights
For more complex telemetry scenarios that need advanced configuration

questions.explanation: Learn recommends the Microsoft OpenTelemetry Distro for new Python projects and points to the Python Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Exporter, a preview (prerelease) package, for more complex scenarios that require advanced configuration. Java components use the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro on their own, and for browsers Learn recommends the Application Insights JavaScript SDK rather than OpenTelemetry.

questions.prompt: A Python service that uses microsoft-opentelemetry must write the current trace ID and span ID into its own audit records. Which TWO expressions return them? Select TWO.

options.text: trace.get_current_span().get_span_context().parent_id
trace.get_current_span().attributes["span_id"]
trace.get_current_span().get_span_context().span_id
trace.get_current_span().get_span_context().trace_id
trace.get_tracer(__name__).get_span_context().trace_id

questions.explanation: Learn's Python snippet reads both IDs from the span context of the current span, using trace.get_current_span().get_span_context() and its trace_id and span_id fields. A tracer creates spans but has no span context of its own, the IDs aren't stored among a span's attributes, and the span context carries no parent ID field.

questions.prompt: Which TWO capabilities does Learn list among the Azure-specific features that the Microsoft OpenTelemetry Distro adds over community OpenTelemetry? Select TWO.

options.text: Application Insights standard metrics
Official Microsoft support for exporting through the OTLP exporter
OpenTelemetry tracing from users' web browsers
Full tail-based sampling in a downstream collector
Microsoft Entra authentication for telemetry ingestion

questions.explanation: Learn's list of Azure-specific features includes Microsoft Entra authentication, Application Insights standard metrics, offline storage with retries, compatible sampling, resource detection and Live Metrics. An OTLP exporter can be added but Microsoft doesn't officially support it, full tail-based sampling isn't supported yet, and Learn doesn't recommend OpenTelemetry in browsers.

questions.prompt: Complete the environment settings for a Python service that calls configure_azure_monitor from azure-monitor-opentelemetry.

slots.text: Stop collecting and exporting logs, and keep traces and metrics: ____=None

options.text: OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER
OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER
OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER

slots.text: Export spans every 2 seconds instead of the default: ____=2000

options.text: OTEL_BLRP_SCHEDULE_DELAY
OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY
OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL

slots.text: Export log records every 10 seconds: ____=10000

options.text: OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY
OTEL_BLRP_SCHEDULE_DELAY
OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL

questions.explanation: Each OTEL_*_EXPORTER variable set to None disables collection of one signal, so OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER stops logs alone. OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY is the tracing export interval in milliseconds (default 5000), while OTEL_BLRP_SCHEDULE_DELAY is the logging one, also in milliseconds. OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL controls how often metrics are exported.

questions.prompt: Match each configure_azure_monitor parameter in azure-monitor-opentelemetry to what it does.

options.text: Formats the log records that are collected
Customizes the metrics that the SDK exports
Sets the OpenTelemetry resource associated with the app
Processes spans before they're exported
Processes log records before they're exported

slots.text: views
log_record_processors
logging_formatter
resource

questions.explanation: The README's parameter table says views customize exported metrics, log_record_processors process log records before export, logging_formatter is a Python logging formatter for collected logs, and resource sets the OpenTelemetry Resource, whose attributes take priority over detected ones. Processing spans before export is the job of span_processors, which isn't one of the four listed here.

questions.prompt: Put the start-up code in order for a Python function app that uses azure-monitor-opentelemetry and must avoid duplicate log telemetry from the Functions worker.

options.text: Remove each handler from the root logger's list of handlers
Create the application's logger and start logging
Get the root logger with logging.getLogger()
Call configure_azure_monitor()

questions.explanation: The Functions worker sends its own logging telemetry, so the README recommends clearing the root logger's handlers and says to do it before any loggers are set up and before configure_azure_monitor() runs. The root logger has to be fetched before its handlers can be removed, and application logging comes last, once the distro is configured.

questions.prompt: Which KQL operator adds a computed column to each row while keeping all the columns already there?

options.text: project
extend
take
summarize

questions.explanation: extend keeps the existing columns and appends the ones you define, which suits ad hoc calculations. project returns just the columns you list (it can also rename or compute them), summarize replaces the rows with grouped results, and take adds no columns at all.

questions.prompt: A query on AppExceptions filters with where OuterMessage has "Timeout", yet it misses rows whose message contains ReadTimeoutError. Why?

options.text: has matches whole terms, and Timeout is a fragment of a longer term
has needs search terms of at least three characters
has works on dynamic columns, and OuterMessage is a string
has is case-sensitive, so Timeout doesn't match other casings

questions.explanation: KQL breaks strings into terms made of runs of letters and digits, and has tests for a whole term, so ReadTimeoutError is one term that isn't equal to Timeout; contains, which matches any substring, finds it. has isn't case-sensitive (has_cs is), Timeout is well over the three-character minimum for the term index, and OuterMessage is a string column, which is what has works on.

questions.prompt: Average request duration looks normal, yet users say some requests are very slow. Which summarize line shows, per 5-minute bucket, the duration that 95 of every 100 AppRequests rows stay under?

options.text: summarize max(DurationMs) by bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
summarize avg(DurationMs) * 0.95 by bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
summarize avg(DurationMs) by bin(TimeGenerated, 5m), OperationName
summarize percentile(DurationMs, 95) by bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)

questions.explanation: percentile(DurationMs, 95) returns the value that 95 percent of the durations fall below, which tracks the slow tail, and bin(TimeGenerated, 5m) groups rows into 5-minute buckets. max reports the single slowest request, which one outlier can set, a scaled average sits below the average itself, and an average per operation name still blends the slow requests with the typical ones.

questions.prompt: Complete the KQL query that counts, for each server the calls went to, the dependency calls made in operations that contain a failed request, counting each call once.

slots.text: AppRequests | where Success == false | join kind=____ (AppDependencies)

options.text: rightanti
leftsemi
rightsemi
OperationId
TimeGenerated
ResultCode

slots.text: | summarize calls = count() by ____

options.text: Target
Data
DependencyType

questions.explanation: A rightsemi join returns the AppDependencies rows that match a row on the left, each once and with the dependency columns, which is exactly the set of calls to count. leftsemi returns AppRequests columns, so there is no Target to group by, and rightanti returns the calls from operations without a failed request. OperationId identifies the root operation that all telemetry in it shares, while timestamps and result codes don't link rows; Target holds the server a call went to, DependencyType its kind (such as HTTP or SQL) and Data the full URL or statement.

questions.prompt: Put the KQL lines in order to chart the hourly count of HTTP dependency calls over the time range set in Log Analytics.

options.text: | render timechart
AppDependencies
| summarize calls = count() by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where DependencyType == "HTTP"

questions.explanation: A query starts from its table, filters early so that later steps handle fewer rows, and aggregates into hourly buckets before charting; DependencyType no longer exists after the summarize. render has to be the last operator, and a timechart takes its x-axis from the first column, which the binned TimeGenerated provides.

questions.prompt: A nightly Python job runs KQL through LogsQueryClient from azure-monitor-query 2.0. Which TWO statements are true? Select TWO.

options.text: A partly failed query returns a result with partial_error and partial_data
The client authenticates with an Application Insights connection string
query_workspace takes the workspace ID, the query and a timespan
MetricsQueryClient in the same package runs the job's metric queries
query_resource needs the workspace ID of a Log Analytics workspace

questions.explanation: query_workspace runs KQL against a Log Analytics workspace by ID over a timespan, and when part of the data can't be returned the result is a LogsQueryPartialResult whose partial_error and partial_data you can inspect. Version 2.0 removed the metrics clients from the package (MetricsClient moved to azure-monitor-querymetrics), the client takes a token credential such as DefaultAzureCredential, and query_resource takes an Azure resource ID with no workspace involved.

questions.prompt: A slow query starts with AppExceptions | where * has "timeout", filters OuterType with =~ and ends with a TimeGenerated filter; the timeout text appears in OuterMessage alone. Which TWO changes make it faster with the same results? Select TWO.

options.text: Replace the =~ comparison with tolower(OuterType) ==
Move the TimeGenerated filter directly after the table name
Add take 100 right after the TimeGenerated filter
Filter on a lowercased copy of OuterMessage computed first
Look for the text in OuterMessage instead of in all columns

questions.explanation: Time filters belong straight after the table because KQL can skip whole shards on datetime columns, and naming the one column that holds the text avoids a full-text scan of all columns. tolower() with == is slower than =~, filtering on a computed column is slower than filtering on the table column, and take 100 returns arbitrary rows, which changes the results.

questions.prompt: A service samples 25 percent of its traces, and a dashboard that runs count() over AppRequests per hour shows about a quarter of the real traffic. Which summarize line gives the real request count?

options.text: summarize count() by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h), ItemCount
summarize max(ItemCount) by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
summarize sum(ItemCount) by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
summarize avg(ItemCount) by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)

questions.explanation: With sampling, each stored row stands for ItemCount original items (about 4 at 25 percent), so adding ItemCount up restores the real request count while count() counts the rows that were kept. The maximum or average of ItemCount gives the sampling factor rather than a total, and grouping by ItemCount still counts kept rows.

questions.prompt: You need the 10 slowest requests in AppRequests. Which line should follow the table name?

options.text: | sort by DurationMs asc | take 10
| sort by DurationMs
| take 10 | sort by DurationMs
| top 10 by DurationMs

questions.explanation: top sorts the whole table on the server and returns the first rows, and its default order is descending, so top 10 by DurationMs gives the ten longest requests. take picks arbitrary rows before anything is sorted, ascending order followed by take returns the fastest ten, and sort by itself returns all rows.

questions.prompt: doc-classifier records each failed classification as an exception in Application Insights. Analysts want a chart of failures per hour with one line for each exception type. Which lines should follow AppExceptions | where AppRoleName == "doc-classifier"?

options.text: | summarize failures = count() by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h), OuterMessage, ExceptionType | render timechart
| summarize failures = count() by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h) | render timechart with (series=ExceptionType)
| summarize failures = count() by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h), ExceptionType | render timechart
| summarize failures = count() by ExceptionType | render timechart

questions.explanation: In Azure Monitor a timechart's first column should be the datetime x-axis, its numeric columns are the y-axes, and one string column groups the values into separate lines, with further string columns ignored. Putting OuterMessage first draws a line per message, grouping by ExceptionType alone gives one total per type with no datetime column for the x-axis and no hourly counts, and the series property names a column that the summarize has already dropped.

questions.prompt: A small share of AppTraces rows from one service appear twice with identical content. What does Learn give as the usual cause of such duplicates in Azure Monitor Logs?

options.text: Sampling stores each kept item twice to preserve the counts
Log Analytics keeps one copy of each row per paired region
The query's time filter overlaps the portal's time picker
Pipeline components retry to make delivery reliable

questions.explanation: Learn's FAQ says duplicates usually come from retries that components in the ingestion pipeline make to ensure reliable delivery, which can duplicate a small percentage of items; on virtual machines, running two agents is the other cause. A time filter only narrows the range, rows aren't copied per region, and sampling represents dropped items through ItemCount rather than duplicating kept ones.

questions.prompt: A query keeps only the AppRequests rows whose OperationId appears in a short list taken from AppExceptions, using join kind=leftsemi on OperationId. What do Learn's best practices recommend instead?
